metadata.notes: Baseline for sift-email using Gmail's Important mark and star, a time-based search for new mail, and a daily review of how the user handles mail (PR #129, issue #128), evals 1-25, two runs each, with run-mcp-trials.sh against the Gmail, Claude Docs, and Contacts stubs. Both runs were on SKILL.md as of commit ed3df62, run in parallel with separate trial directories under $TMPDIR. Eval 11 in both runs comes from a rerun on the same SKILL.md after its fixture began dating its already-ran daily review by the trial's own clock ({{today:America/Chicago}}): the first pair ran just after midnight in Chicago, so the review was due and the eval did not test the cheap exit. Every eval prompt starts with /sift-email. Runs were on 2026-10-25 in the rubric timezone; fixtures are anchored to 2026-10-10 and shifted two weeks by fixture-dates.py, and graders held the run date to the date the run's clock gave. Failures: eval 7 run 1 (added a changelog entry for its own (inferred) About me notes, against an expectation that the changelog stays unchanged), eval 8 run 1 (removed IMPORTANT from the thread the user had marked before fetching it, then restored it; the end state is right), and eval 23 run 2 (labeled an unsolicited sale Bulk, reading the list's 'you subscribed' footer as a relationship). Not graded: the Bulk and Junk split for marketing and list mail varies between runs (eval 21's sale, eval 19's potluck); (inferred) About me notes sometimes replace the template's placeholder topic; the Daily review note usually sits in the run summary rather than on its own line; log summaries sometimes miscount; and unrequested category labels.
